# Control Narrative: Ammonia Screw Compressor C-101

**Document status:** DRAFT for owner and integrator review
**PLC:** Allen-Bradley CompactLogix | **HMI:** Engine room office

> **Notation.** Values marked **[P]** are proposed by the author, not given in the process data. The owner and the compressor manufacturer must confirm or replace each one before coding. Items marked **[OPEN]** are listed in Section 16 and must be resolved before FAT.

---

## 1. Scope

This narrative covers control and protection of screw compressor C-101. It includes:

- capacity (slide valve) control
- start and stop sequencing
- alarms and shutdowns
- ammonia detection response for the machine room
- emergency shutdown (ESD) of the machine room

It defines the logic the integrator will code and the behaviour the FAT witness will verify. The test procedures are in Section 15.

This document does not replace:

- the compressor manufacturer's protection requirements
- IIAR 2 / ASHRAE 15 / local mechanical and fire code requirements
- the facility PHA

Where those conflict with this narrative, the more stringent requirement governs, and this narrative shall be revised.

## 2. Abbreviations

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| FLA | Motor full-load amps (nameplate value, entered as a setpoint) |
| SV | Slide valve |
| ESD | Emergency shutdown |
| First-out | The first trip condition to occur, latched and displayed separately from trips that follow it |
| Latched | Stays active after the condition clears, until an operator resets it |
| psid | Pounds per square inch, differential |

## 3. Equipment and I/O

| Tag | Description | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-101 | 400 hp screw compressor | — | Across-the-line soft starter, no VFD |
| PT-101 | Suction pressure | AI 4–20 mA | Range **[P]** -15 to 100 psig |
| PDT-102 | Oil differential pressure | AI 4–20 mA | Range **[P]** 0–150 psid. The reference point (oil manifold minus suction, or minus discharge) is per the manufacturer **[OPEN]** |
| TT-103 | Discharge temperature | AI 4–20 mA / RTD | Range **[P]** 0–300 °F |
| II-104 | Motor current (CT via transducer) | AI 4–20 mA | Range **[P]** 0–150% FLA |
| ZT-101 | Slide valve position | AI 4–20 mA | **[OPEN]** Not in the process data, but required for the start-unloaded permissive and position display. 0–100% |
| SV-LOAD | Slide valve load solenoid | DO | Pulsed |
| SV-UNLD | Slide valve unload solenoid | DO | Pulsed |
| C-101-RUN | Soft starter run command | DO | Interposing relay. Contact is in series with the hardwired ESD string (Section 11) |
| C-101-RF | Soft starter run feedback | DI | |
| C-101-UTS | Soft starter up-to-speed / bypass closed | DI | |
| C-101-FLT | Soft starter fault | DI | Fail-safe (open = fault) |
| AE-110A / AE-110B | Machine room NH₃ detectors | AI 4–20 mA (or relay outputs from the gas controller) | Range **[P]** 0–300 ppm. See Section 10.4 |
| EF-201 | Emergency exhaust fan | DO (high-speed command), DI (run feedback) | |
| XV-120 | Machine room main liquid solenoid | DO | Energize-to-open, fail-closed. Contact is in series with the hardwired ESD string |
| HS-ESD | Break-glass ESD station, outside the machine room | Hardwired + DI monitor | Fail-safe (open = ESD) |

**I/O rule.** All shutdown-related digital inputs shall be fail-safe (normally closed, open = abnormal). All analog inputs shall have out-of-range detection per Section 12.

## 4. Operating Modes

C-101 has three HMI-selectable modes. Changing mode requires an Operator login or higher.

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **OFF** | Compressor cannot start. If running, it performs a normal stop (Section 8). |
| **MANUAL** | Operator starts and stops from the HMI. The operator jogs the slide valve with Load/Unload buttons, each pulse lasting **[P]** 0.5 s. **All trips, permissives, current limit, and forced-unload overrides remain active.** |
| **AUTO** | Operator starts and stops from the HMI. After the start sequence completes, the slide valve is controlled on suction pressure (Section 7). |

- **Auto start/stop on demand** (starting on rising suction and stopping on low load) is **not** included. **[OPEN]**: confirm whether it is required, and whether C-101 joins a lead/lag scheme with the existing compressors.
- **Bumpless transfer.** Switching between MANUAL and AUTO while running does not move the slide valve. Control resumes from the current position.

## 5. Start Permissives

All permissives must be true to start. The HMI shall show each one with a green or red indicator, so the operator can see why a start is blocked.

| # | Permissive |
|---|---|
| P1 | Mode is MANUAL or AUTO |
| P2 | No latched trip on C-101 (all trips reset) |
| P3 | Hardwired ESD circuit healthy (HS-ESD monitor closed, ESD relay energized) |
| P4 | No 150 ppm NH₃ shutdown active or latched |
| P5 | Both NH₃ detectors healthy (no fault). **[OPEN]**: see 10.4 |
| P6 | Soft starter ready (C-101-FLT healthy, run feedback off) |
| P7 | Starts-per-hour count below limit (Section 9) |
| P8 | Minimum off time elapsed: **[P]** 5 min since last stop |
| P9 | Slide valve at minimum: ZT-101 ≤ **[P]** 5% |
| P10 | PT-101 > 2 psig trip setpoint + **[P]** 2 psi |
| P11 | TT-103 < 190 °F alarm setpoint |
| P12 | No instrument fault on PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104, ZT-101 |
| P13 | **[OPEN]** Oil level / oil heater / pre-lube permissives, per the manufacturer |

P9 handling: if all permissives except P9 are true, a start request first drives the slide valve to minimum (see 6.1).

## 6. Start Sequence

| Step | Action | Proceed when | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | If ZT-101 > 5%, energize SV-UNLD continuously | ZT-101 ≤ 5% | Not reached in **[P]** 120 s: abort, alarm "C-101 Failed to Unload" |
| 6.2 | **[OPEN]** Pre-lube oil pump, if fitted | Per manufacturer | Per manufacturer |
| 6.3 | Energize C-101-RUN. **Increment the start counter now** (Section 9). Start the 30 s low-oil bypass timer. | C-101-RF on within **[P]** 3 s | Trip "C-101 Fail to Start" |
| 6.4 | Wait for soft starter ramp | C-101-UTS on within **[P]** 30 s | Trip "C-101 Fail to Reach Speed" |
| 6.5 | Hold slide valve at minimum (load inhibited) | Bypass timer done (30 s from step 6.3) **and** PDT-102 ≥ 35 psid | At 30 s the low-oil trip arms; if PDT-102 < 25 psid it trips per Section 10.1 |
| 6.6 | Release slide valve to MANUAL or AUTO control. Status: "Running" | — | — |

The low-oil **alarm** (35 psid) is also suppressed during the 30 s bypass. All other trips are active from the moment C-101-RUN is energized.

## 7. Capacity Control (AUTO)

### 7.1 Suction pressure control

- **Setpoint SP-101:** default 15 psig, adjustable 5–30 psig.
  - Changes require a **Supervisor** login.
  - Entries outside 5–30 psig are rejected with a message.
  - Every change is logged with user, time, old value, and new value.
- **Error:** E = PT-101 − SP-101. Positive error means suction is too high, so the compressor loads.
- **Deadband:** DB = **[P]** ±0.5 psi. Supervisor-adjustable over **[P]** 0.2–2.0 psi.
- **Pulse cycle:** fixed period T = **[P]** 10 s. In each cycle:

| Condition | Output |
|---|---|
| E > +DB | One SV-LOAD pulse |
| E < −DB | One SV-UNLD pulse |
| \|E\| ≤ DB | No pulse |

- **Pulse width** scales linearly with \|E\|:
  - Minimum **[P]** 0.2 s at \|E\| = DB
  - Maximum **[P]** 2.0 s at \|E\| ≥ DB + 5 psi
  - Tuning parameters (T, minimum width, maximum width) are adjustable at Engineer level only.
- **Interlock:** SV-LOAD and SV-UNLD shall never be energized at the same time. This must be enforced in logic, and by hardware interlock if the manufacturer requires it.
- **Position limits:**
  - At ZT-101 ≥ **[P]** 99%, stop load pulses.
  - At the minimum stop (≤ **[P]** 10%), stop unload pulses unless the stop sequence (Section 8) or start sequence (step 6.1) is driving to the hard minimum.
  - Process data gives the range as 10–100%. **[OPEN]**: confirm whether 10% is the minimum mechanical stop, and whether the start permissive should therefore be ≤ 10% rather than ≤ 5%.

### 7.2 Overrides

Overrides apply in **both AUTO and MANUAL**. Priority is highest first; a higher override always wins.

| Priority | Override | Activates at | Releases at | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Any trip | Section 10 | Reset | Stop motor, de-energize SV outputs |
| 2 | Current forced unload | II-104 ≥ **[P]** 100% FLA for 2 s | II-104 < 95% FLA | Continuous unload pulses (**[P]** 1 s on / 2 s off). Alarm "C-101 Current Limit Unloading" |
| 3 | Low suction forced unload | PT-101 ≤ **[P]** 4 psig | PT-101 ≥ **[P]** 5 psig | Continuous unload pulses as above. Alarm "C-101 Low Suction Unloading" |
| 4 | **Current load inhibit** | II-104 ≥ **95% FLA** | II-104 < **[P]** 92% FLA | Block all load pulses. Unload is still allowed. HMI status "Current Limit" |
| 5 | Start hold | Steps 6.1–6.5 | Step 6.6 | Block all load pulses |
| 6 | **[P]** Alarm load inhibit | PDT-102 low alarm or TT-103 high alarm active | Alarm clears | Block load pulses |
| 7 | Normal control | — | — | Section 7.1 |

- **FLA setpoint:** an Engineer-level setpoint entered from the motor nameplate. It must be entered and verified before FAT.
- **Requirement met:** "must not load above 95% FLA" is satisfied by Priority 4. Priority 2 is a proposed backstop in case current continues to rise without loading, for example from rising discharge pressure.

## 8. Normal Stop

A normal stop is triggered by the operator Stop button, or by selecting OFF while running.

1. Block load pulses. Energize SV-UNLD continuously until ZT-101 ≤ minimum, or **[P]** 60 s elapses.
2. De-energize C-101-RUN.
3. Confirm C-101-RF is off within **[P]** 5 s. If not, raise the alarm "C-101 Fail to Stop – Check Starter".
4. Start the minimum off timer (P8).

A second press of Stop during step 1 stops the motor immediately.

## 9. Starts-Per-Hour Limit

- The PLC keeps time stamps of the last 4 starts. A start is counted when C-101-RUN is energized, including failed starts.
- If 4 starts have occurred within the last 60 minutes (a rolling window, not a clock hour), permissive P7 is false.
- The HMI shows:
  - starts in the last 60 minutes
  - time remaining until the next start is allowed
- The time stamps must survive a PLC power cycle. Store them in non-volatile tags, or treat a power-up as "4 starts occurred at power-up time" **[OPEN – owner choice]**.
- The PLC limit (4/hr) shall be set equal to or more restrictive than the soft starter's internal limit. **[OPEN]**: confirm the soft starter's own setting.
- There is no operator bypass. Engineer-level bypass is **[P]** not provided.

## 10. Alarms and Shutdowns

### 10.1 C-101 protection

| ID | Tag | Condition | Setpoint | Delay | Active when | Action | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | PDT-102 | Low oil diff alarm | < 35 psid | **[P]** 5 s | Running, after 30 s bypass | Alarm + Priority 6 load inhibit | Auto-clears at ≥ **[P]** 37 psid; acknowledge required |
| T1 | PDT-102 | Low oil diff trip | < 25 psid | **[P]** 3 s | Running, after 30 s bypass | **Trip C-101** | Manual, after condition clears |
| A2 | TT-103 | High discharge temp alarm | > 190 °F | **[P]** 5 s | Always | Alarm + Priority 6 load inhibit | Auto-clears at ≤ **[P]** 185 °F; acknowledge required |
| T2 | TT-103 | High discharge temp trip | > 210 °F | **[P]** 3 s | Always | **Trip C-101** | Manual, after TT-103 < 190 °F |
| T3 | PT-101 | Low suction trip | < 2 psig | **[P]** 5 s | Running | **Trip C-101** | Manual |
| A3 | II-104 | Current limit | ≥ 95% FLA | 0 s | Running | Priority 4 load inhibit; status only | Auto |
| T4 | C-101-RF | Fail to start / reach speed / unexpected loss of run | Section 6, or RF lost while commanded | Per Section 6; 1 s for loss | Running | **Trip C-101** | Manual |
| T5 | C-101-FLT | Soft starter fault | Input open | 0.5 s | Always | **Trip C-101** | Manual (clear fault at starter first) |
| T6 | Analog | Instrument fault | Section 12 | Section 12 | Section 12 | Section 12 | Manual |
| T7 | Gas | NH₃ high-high | Section 10.2 | — | Always | **Trip ALL compressors** + close XV-120 | Section 10.2 |
| T8 | ESD | ESD | Section 11 | — | Always | **Trip ALL** (hardwired) | Section 11 |

**General rules:**

- **Delays.** All delays and hystereses are **[P]** and must be checked against the compressor manufacturer's requirements before coding. In particular, confirm whether the manufacturer requires the low-oil trip delay to be shorter.
- **Trip action:**
  - de-energize C-101-RUN immediately (no unload first)
  - de-energize both SV outputs
  - latch the trip
  - record first-out
  - sound the HMI audible alarm
- **No automatic restart after any trip.** Restarting requires: condition cleared → operator Reset (Operator login) → new Start command.
- **First-out.** The HMI shows which trip occurred first, with a time stamp. Later trips are listed but not flagged as first-out.

### 10.2 Machine room ammonia detection

Voting: **1oo2.** Either AE-110A or AE-110B exceeding a setpoint triggers the action.

| Level | Setpoint | Delay | Action | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **High** | ≥ 25 ppm | **[P]** 0 s, or the detector manufacturer's response time | 1. HMI alarm, plus local audible/visual beacons at the machine room entrance and inside the room **[OPEN]** for beacon I/O. 2. Command EF-201 to **high speed**. Latched. | EF-201 remains at high speed until **both** detectors read < **[P]** 20 ppm **and** an operator presses "Reset Ventilation" (Operator login) |
| **High-High** | ≥ 150 ppm | **[P]** 0 s | 1. Alarm. 2. **Trip ALL compressors** in the machine room, not only C-101 **[OPEN]**: list which existing compressors and how each is tripped. 3. **De-energize XV-120** (closes). 4. EF-201 continues at high speed, and is **not** stopped by this shutdown. | Manual reset only, after both detectors < 25 ppm. Supervisor login **[P]** |

- **EF-201 run confirmation.** If EF-201 is commanded but run feedback is not received within **[P]** 10 s, raise the alarm "EF-201 Fail to Run".
- **Code check required.** IIAR 2, ASHRAE 15, and the local fire and mechanical codes specify detection levels, required actions, and alarm locations for ammonia machinery rooms. These may require responses beyond those listed, such as alarms outside the room or at a constantly attended location, or ventilation activation at a specific level. The owner's setpoints above shall be reconciled against the applicable code edition and the AHJ before issue. **[OPEN]**

### 10.3 XV-120

- XV-120 is energized only when all of the following are true:
  - no ESD
  - no 150 ppm shutdown latched
  - **[P]** an operator-enable signal from the HMI is present
- XV-120 is normally open in operation. Stopping C-101 alone does not close XV-120, because the valve serves the whole machine room **[OPEN]: confirm**.

### 10.4 Detector fault handling **[OPEN – owner decision required]**

The gas detection controller signals a detector fault by either of:

- analog signal < 3.5 mA or > 21 mA
- a dedicated fault contact

Proposed fail-safe response:

- **One detector faulted:**
  - alarm "AE-110x Fault"
  - start EF-201 at high speed (treated as a 25 ppm condition)
  - compressors keep running on the remaining detector
- **Both detectors faulted:**
  - alarm
  - EF-201 high speed
  - **[P]** trip all compressors and close XV-120 (no machine-room gas monitoring remains)

**Hardwiring recommendation.** The 150 ppm shutdown should not depend only on the PLC. The gas detection controller's high-high relay should be wired directly into the ESD string (Section 11), with the PLC monitoring it. If the owner accepts a PLC-only 150 ppm shutdown, record that decision and its PHA basis here.

## 11. Emergency Shutdown (Hardwired)

### 11.1 Circuit

- The break-glass station HS-ESD, located outside the machine room, is wired in a fail-safe series loop with:
  - a master ESD relay
  - **[recommended]** the gas controller's 150 ppm relay contact
- **Loop open** (glass broken, wire cut, or loss of control power): the master ESD relay de-energizes.
- **The master ESD relay de-energizing directly:**
  - opens the run circuit of **every** machine room compressor starter, including C-101
  - opens the coil circuit of XV-120
- **This action does not pass through PLC logic.** The PLC run outputs are wired in series downstream of the ESD relay contacts.

### 11.2 PLC role (monitoring only)

- The PLC monitors HS-ESD and the ESD relay status through DIs.
- On ESD, the PLC:
  1. latches an ESD alarm, recorded as first-out
  2. drops all compressor run outputs and SV outputs, so nothing restarts when the loop is restored
  3. de-energizes the XV-120 output
- **ESD does not stop EF-201.** Emergency ventilation remains available. **[OPEN]**: confirm whether a separate emergency ventilation manual switch is also required outside the room, per code.

### 11.3 Reset

1. Replace the glass or reset the station, which closes the loop.
2. Reset the master ESD relay. This requires deliberate action at the relay panel **[P]**, and the relay must not auto-reset.
3. Perform a Supervisor-level PLC reset at the HMI.
4. Restart compressors individually by operator command.

## 12. Instrument Failure Handling

An analog input is "faulted" when any of these persist for **[P]** 2 s:

- signal < 3.8 mA or > 20.5 mA
- module or channel fault
- loss of communication

| Instrument | Fault response |
|---|---|
| PT-101 | **Trip C-101.** Low suction protection and capacity control are both lost |
| PDT-102 | **Trip C-101** |
| TT-103 | **Trip C-101** |
| II-104 | Alarm. Block loading. Hold position. **[P]**: alternatively, trip. Owner to choose |
| ZT-101 | Alarm. Running compressor continues in AUTO, with the 99% position limit replaced by the current limit only. Start not permitted while faulted |
| AE-110A/B | Section 10.4 |
| PLC/CPU fault, or loss of HMI communication | Outputs fail to de-energized state, so the compressor stops and XV-120 closes. The hardwired ESD is unaffected. Loss of HMI communication alone does **not** stop the compressor; raise an alarm when communication returns. **[P]** |

## 13. Power Failure and Restart

- On loss of power, all outputs de-energize.
- On power restoration:
  - the compressor stays stopped
  - the HMI shows "Power Restored – Restart Required"
  - **no automatic restart**
- The starts-per-hour record is handled per Section 9.
- **[OPEN]**: confirm whether the owner wants automatic restart after a power failure, for example for unattended night operation. If so, add a staggered restart delay and confirm it with the code and the PHA.

## 14. HMI Requirements

### 14.1 Overview display

- C-101 status: Stopped / Starting / Running / Stopping / Tripped / Locked Out (starts limit)
- Mode
- Live values: PT-101, SP-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104 (amps and % FLA), ZT-101, AE-110A/B ppm
- Status of EF-201, XV-120, and ESD
- Active override (Priority 2–6) shown as text
- Starts in the last 60 minutes, and time until the next start is allowed
- Permissive list (Section 5)

### 14.2 Alarms

- Alarm summary showing active and unacknowledged alarms
- First-out display
- Alarm and event history, kept for **[P]** a minimum of 90 days

### 14.3 Trends

- Trend of PT-101, SP-101, II-104, ZT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, AE-110A/B
- **[P]** 1 s sample rate, 30-day retention

### 14.4 Security levels

| Level | Permissions |
|---|---|
| Operator | Start, Stop, Mode, Acknowledge, Reset of C-101 trips, Reset Ventilation |
| Supervisor | Change SP-101 (5–30 psig) and deadband. Reset NH₃ high-high and ESD |
| Engineer | FLA, pulse tuning, alarm delays and hystereses, override setpoints |

**Trip setpoints** (25 psid, 210 °F, 2 psig, 150 ppm) are **not** HMI-adjustable. They are fixed in PLC code, and changing them requires management-of-change.

All setpoint changes and resets shall be logged with user and time stamp.

## 15. FAT Test Procedure (Summary)

### 15.1 Test conditions

- Use simulated signals: mA source on the analog inputs, jumpers or switches on the discrete inputs.
- Use a simulated starter, with feedback looped back.
- For each test, the witness records pass or fail, the values observed, and initials.

### 15.2 Tests

| # | Test | Method | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | I/O check | Exercise each point; verify tag, range, and engineering units on the HMI | All points match the I/O list. Analog values within ±0.5% span |
| F2 | Permissives | Defeat each permissive P1–P12 in turn | Start blocked; correct permissive shown red |
| F3 | Start, unloaded | Set ZT-101 = 50% and press Start | SV-UNLD energizes; motor does not start until ZT ≤ 5%. With ZT held at 50% for 120 s: "Failed to Unload", no start |
| F4 | Normal start | All permissives true | Sequence per Section 6. Start counter increments. Load inhibited until 30 s **and** PDT ≥ 35 |
| F5 | Fail to start / fail to reach speed | Withhold RF; separately, withhold UTS | Trip with correct message, first-out, and timings |
| F6 | Low oil bypass | Hold PDT-102 at 10 psid through start | No alarm or trip during the first 30 s. Trip T1 at 30 s + 3 s |
| F7 | Low oil alarm/trip | After bypass, ramp PDT down | Alarm at < 35 (5 s delay) with load inhibit. Trip at < 25 (3 s delay) |
| F8 | Discharge temp | Ramp TT-103 | Alarm at > 190 °F (5 s); trip at > 210 °F (3 s); reset blocked until < 190 °F |
| F9 | Low suction | Ramp PT-101 down | Forced unload at ≤ 4; release at ≥ 5; trip at < 2 psig (5 s) |
| F10 | Capacity control | SP = 15. Step PT-101 to 16, 20, 14, 10, 15.3 | Load/unload pulses in the correct direction, widths per 7.1, none inside deadband. Never both outputs on together |
| F11 | Setpoint security | Enter SP 4, 31, 20 as Operator, then as Supervisor | Operator rejected. Supervisor: 4 and 31 rejected, 20 accepted and logged |
| F12 | Current limit | Ramp II-104 while the controller is calling to load | Load pulses stop at 95% FLA; resume below 92%. Forced unload at ≥ 100% for 2 s |
| F13 | Override priority | Apply low suction + current limit + controller load demand together | Highest priority wins per 7.2 |
| F14 | Starts limit | Perform 4 starts | 5th start blocked; countdown correct; start allowed 60 min after the 1st. Repeat with a PLC power cycle |
| F15 | Normal stop | Press Stop while loaded | Unloads, then stops. Second Stop press stops immediately |
| F16 | NH₃ 25 ppm | Inject 25 ppm on A only, then B only | Alarm, EF-201 high speed, latched. Reset blocked until both < 20 ppm |
| F17 | NH₃ 150 ppm | Inject on A only, then B only | All compressors trip, XV-120 closes, EF-201 stays at high speed. Repeat with the PLC in program mode, if hardwired per 10.4 |
| F18 | Detector fault | Set AE-110A to 2 mA; then both | Per Section 10.4 |
| F19 | ESD | Open HS-ESD loop: (a) with PLC running, (b) with PLC in program mode or CPU removed | In both cases the compressor run circuit and XV-120 de-energize, and EF-201 is unaffected. Restoring the loop does not restart anything. Reset per 11.3 |
| F20 | Instrument faults | Open-circuit each analog input | Response per Section 12 |
| F21 | Soft starter fault | Open C-101-FLT while running | Immediate trip |
| F22 | Power fail | Cycle PLC power while running | Stops; no auto restart; message shown |
| F23 | Manual mode | Run in MANUAL; repeat F7, F8, F12 | All protections and overrides still active |
| F24 | First-out | Trigger T2 then T1 in sequence | T2 shown as first-out |

## 16. Open Items (to resolve before coding or FAT)

1. **High discharge pressure cutout.** None is listed. Code requires a hardwired high-pressure safety cutout on the compressor. Add it as a hardwired trip in the starter circuit with PLC monitoring, plus a PLC alarm and trip from a discharge PT if one is fitted.
2. **Other manufacturer protections.** Confirm the manufacturer's full list and add those that apply: oil filter ΔP, oil temperature, oil level, motor winding temperature, high motor current, oil separator level, and vibration if fitted.
3. **Slide valve position transmitter.** Confirm ZT-101 exists, and define the minimum stop position (5% vs 10%).
4. **PDT-102 reference.** Confirm the oil differential reference definition and the manufacturer's trip delay.
5. **Pre-lube oil pump.** Confirm whether one is fitted, and its sequence if so.
6. **Gas response vs code.** Reconcile the gas detection setpoints and actions with IIAR 2 / ASHRAE 15 / local code and the AHJ, including alarm annunciation locations.
7. **Hardwired 150 ppm.** Decide whether the 150 ppm shutdown is hardwired (recommended) or PLC-only.
8. **Detector fault response.** Decide the response per Section 10.4.
9. **"All compressors."** List the existing compressors and their trip interface. Confirm that the master ESD relay contacts reach each starter.
10. **XV-120.** Confirm its enable logic, and whether stopping only C-101 should close it.
11. **Soft starter limit.** Confirm the soft starter's internal starts limit, and the starts-record behaviour on power loss.
12. **Auto operation.** Decide on auto start/stop, lead/lag, and auto restart after power failure.
13. **II-104 fault.** Decide whether the response is hold or trip.
14. **Proposed values.** Confirm every value marked [P].
15. **Separate ventilation switch.** Confirm whether a separate emergency ventilation switch outside the room is required.

---

*This narrative should be reviewed by the refrigeration engineer of record and covered in the facility PHA/MOC before issue for construction.*
